title_slide: Dance Anyway: On Permission, Audiences, and the Things We Almost Delete

slides.heading: The Quote Has a Dark Sequel
bullet_points: 'Dance like nobody's watching' — you've heard it
Here's what nobody adds: eventually, people watch
And then the watching changes everything
slides.speaker_note: Open with the paradox — don't resolve it yet, just name it.

slides.heading: The 6-Second Video
bullet_points: 11pm, alone, doing something embarrassing
Almost deleted it before anyone saw
It became the most authentic thing I'd ever posted
slides.speaker_note: Ground the abstract in a real moment — specificity earns trust.

slides.heading: What the Best Pieces Have in Common
bullet_points: Mid-thought, not fully formed
Almost didn't post
No framework — just honest
slides.speaker_note: Name the pattern directly before explaining it.

slides.heading: Unselfconsciousness
bullet_points: The hardest creative skill
Not about talent — about forgetting to care
Our brains are engineered to monitor ourselves
slides.speaker_note: Name the concept and humanize why it's hard — removes shame from the struggle.

slides.heading: The Paradox
bullet_points: Authentic act → audience → mirror → self-consciousness
Suddenly the dance is choreographed
It wasn't supposed to be
slides.speaker_note: This is the sharpest idea — slow down here, don't rush past the discomfort.

slides.heading: The Small Practice
bullet_points: One thing per week with no audience
Not a draft, not a future post
Keeps your center of gravity low
slides.speaker_note: Offer something actionable — not a fix, a practice. The distinction matters.

slides.heading: Dance Anyway
bullet_points: The room won't clear
Applause doesn't arrive in advance
Self-consciousness only disappears inside the doing
slides.speaker_note: Close without a bow — land on the truth, not a prescription.
